title: Food & Dairy Microbiology
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Food & Dairy Microbiology curriculum: microbial food spoilage, food preservation methods, fermented foods and starter cultures, dairy microbiology (milk composition, souring, cheese/yoghurt production), food-borne infection and intoxication, indicator organisms and food safety systems (HACCP), and probiotics.

questions.question: Food spoilage caused by microbial growth is generally most rapid in foods that are:
options: Low in moisture (low water activity), acidic, and stored cold
High in moisture (high water activity), near-neutral pH, and stored at warm temperatures
Completely sterile
Packaged under vacuum with no oxygen at all
questions.correct_answer: High in moisture (high water activity), near-neutral pH, and stored at warm temperatures
questions.explanation: Microbial growth in food is favoured by high water activity, near-neutral pH, ample nutrients, and warm temperatures; foods lacking these conditions (dried, acidic, chilled) spoil more slowly because microbial growth is inhibited.

questions.question: Water activity (aw) in food microbiology refers to:
options: The total water content of a food by weight
The ratio of the vapour pressure of water in a food to the vapour pressure of pure water at the same temperature, reflecting the water available for microbial growth
The pH of the food
The oxygen concentration dissolved in the food
questions.correct_answer: The ratio of the vapour pressure of water in a food to the vapour pressure of pure water at the same temperature, reflecting the water available for microbial growth
questions.explanation: Water activity measures the free, unbound water available to microorganisms rather than total moisture content; most bacteria require aw above about 0.90-0.91 to grow, while molds and some yeasts can grow at lower aw, so reducing aw is a key preservation principle.

questions.question: Which group of microorganisms is generally most tolerant of low water activity and can spoil dried or sugary/salty foods that bacteria cannot grow on?
options: Molds (and some osmotolerant/xerotolerant yeasts)
Obligate anaerobic bacteria
Vibrio species
Lactic acid bacteria
questions.correct_answer: Molds (and some osmotolerant/xerotolerant yeasts)
questions.explanation: Molds generally tolerate lower water activity than bacteria, and certain xerotolerant/osmotolerant yeasts and molds can grow on dried fruits, jams, and other low-moisture or high-sugar foods where bacterial growth is inhibited.

questions.question: Pseudomonas species are common spoilage organisms of refrigerated fresh meat, fish, and milk mainly because they are:
options: Thermophilic and cannot grow below 30°C
Psychrotrophic (able to grow at refrigeration temperatures) and produce proteolytic and lipolytic enzymes that cause off-odours, slime, and spoilage
Strict anaerobes that cannot grow in air
Endospore-forming and heat resistant
questions.correct_answer: Psychrotrophic (able to grow at refrigeration temperatures) and produce proteolytic and lipolytic enzymes that cause off-odours, slime, and spoilage
questions.explanation: Pseudomonas species grow well at refrigeration temperatures and secrete extracellular proteases and lipases, causing characteristic slime, off-flavours, and odours in chilled meat, fish, and dairy products.

questions.question: Canning as a food preservation method relies principally on:
options: Adding preservative chemicals only
Heat treatment sufficient to destroy microorganisms (including heat-resistant spores of concern like Clostridium botulinum) combined with hermetic (airtight) sealing to prevent recontamination
Freezing the food solid
Reducing the pH of the food to below 2
questions.correct_answer: Heat treatment sufficient to destroy microorganisms (including heat-resistant spores of concern like Clostridium botulinum) combined with hermetic (airtight) sealing to prevent recontamination
questions.explanation: Commercial canning uses heat processing calibrated to achieve commercial sterility, notably eliminating the risk from Clostridium botulinum spores in low-acid canned foods, then seals the container airtight to prevent subsequent microbial entry.

questions.question: The 'botulinum cook' (12D process) applied to low-acid canned foods is designed to reduce the probability of surviving Clostridium botulinum spores to:
options: One in a thousand cans
A theoretical probability of one surviving spore in 10^12 containers processed
Zero risk is impossible so no standard exists
Fifty percent of the original spore load
questions.correct_answer: A theoretical probability of one surviving spore in 10^12 containers processed
questions.explanation: The standard '12D' botulinum cook is designed to achieve a 12-log reduction in C. botulinum spores, corresponding to a theoretical survival probability of about one spore in 10^12 containers, an extremely high margin of safety for low-acid canned foods.

questions.question: Sun-drying and dehydration preserve foods primarily by:
options: Killing all microorganisms present instantly
Reducing water activity below the level required for microbial growth, thereby inhibiting spoilage and pathogenic organisms
Increasing the food's pH
Adding preservative salts
questions.correct_answer: Reducing water activity below the level required for microbial growth, thereby inhibiting spoilage and pathogenic organisms
questions.explanation: Drying lowers water activity to a point where most spoilage and pathogenic microorganisms cannot grow (though many may survive in a dormant state), extending shelf life without necessarily sterilising the food.

questions.question: Curing of meats with salt and/or nitrate/nitrite preserves the product mainly by:
options: Increasing water activity to favour beneficial bacteria
Lowering water activity (via salt) and, with nitrite, specifically inhibiting Clostridium botulinum outgrowth and toxin formation, while also contributing to colour and flavour
Sterilising the meat completely
Removing all fat content
questions.correct_answer: Lowering water activity (via salt) and, with nitrite, specifically inhibiting Clostridium botulinum outgrowth and toxin formation, while also contributing to colour and flavour
questions.explanation: Curing salts reduce water activity and nitrite specifically suppresses germination and toxin production by Clostridium botulinum spores, while also fixing the characteristic pink cured colour and contributing antioxidant/flavour effects.

questions.question: Irradiation of food for preservation typically uses which type of radiation to reduce microbial load without significantly heating the product?
options: Visible light
Ionising radiation, such as gamma rays from cobalt-60
Infrared heat lamps
Microwave radiation only
questions.correct_answer: Ionising radiation, such as gamma rays from cobalt-60
questions.explanation: Food irradiation uses ionising radiation (gamma rays, electron beams, or X-rays) to damage microbial DNA and reduce populations of spoilage and pathogenic organisms, largely as a 'cold' process without substantially raising the food's temperature.

questions.question: Modified atmosphere packaging (MAP), commonly used to extend the shelf life of fresh produce and meats, works by:
options: Replacing the air around the food with a gas mixture (often reduced O2, elevated CO2) that slows the growth of aerobic spoilage organisms and the food's own respiration
Filling the package entirely with pure oxygen to speed microbial growth
Removing all packaging materials
Adding preservative chemicals directly into the food
questions.correct_answer: Replacing the air around the food with a gas mixture (often reduced O2, elevated CO2) that slows the growth of aerobic spoilage organisms and the food's own respiration
questions.explanation: MAP alters the gas composition surrounding food, typically lowering oxygen and raising CO2, which suppresses aerobic microbial growth and oxidative spoilage while also slowing the respiration rate of fresh produce.

questions.question: Lactic acid bacteria (e.g. Lactobacillus, Streptococcus, Leuconostoc species) are central to many fermented foods mainly because they:
options: Produce large amounts of ethanol as their primary product
Ferment sugars to lactic acid, lowering the food's pH, which preserves it and imparts characteristic sour flavour and texture
Require strictly anaerobic, oxygen-free environments to survive
Produce toxins that are later removed by cooking
questions.correct_answer: Ferment sugars to lactic acid, lowering the food's pH, which preserves it and imparts characteristic sour flavour and texture
questions.explanation: Lactic acid bacteria convert fermentable sugars mainly to lactic acid, acidifying the food matrix; this acidification both preserves the product by inhibiting spoilage/pathogenic organisms and produces the tangy flavour typical of fermented foods like yoghurt and sauerkraut.

questions.question: Yoghurt is traditionally produced by fermenting milk with a defined starter culture consisting mainly of:
options: Saccharomyces cerevisiae alone
Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus, growing symbiotically
Penicillium roqueforti
Acetobacter aceti
questions.correct_answer: Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus, growing symbiotically
questions.explanation: Standard yoghurt fermentation uses a symbiotic starter culture of Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus, which stimulate each other's growth and jointly produce the lactic acid, texture, and flavour compounds characteristic of yoghurt.

questions.question: In cheese-making, rennet (or microbial/chymosin-based coagulants) is added to milk primarily to:
options: Kill all bacteria in the milk
Coagulate milk casein proteins, forming a curd that is separated from the liquid whey
Lower the fat content of the milk
Sterilise the cheese vat
questions.correct_answer: Coagulate milk casein proteins, forming a curd that is separated from the liquid whey
questions.explanation: Rennet's active enzyme (chymosin) cleaves kappa-casein, destabilising the casein micelle structure and causing the milk proteins to coagulate into a curd, which is then cut, drained of whey, and further processed into cheese.

questions.question: The characteristic blue-green veining and pungent flavour of Roquefort and similar blue cheeses result from ripening by:
options: Penicillium roqueforti
Lactobacillus acidophilus
Propionibacterium freudenreichii
Saccharomyces cerevisiae
questions.correct_answer: Penicillium roqueforti
questions.explanation: Penicillium roqueforti spores are introduced into the cheese and, as the mold grows through air channels in the curd during ripening, its blue-green conidia and lipolytic/proteolytic enzymes create the characteristic veining, texture, and sharp flavour.

questions.question: The characteristic large 'eyes' (holes) in Swiss-type cheeses such as Emmental are produced by:
options: Physical injection of air bubbles during moulding
Carbon dioxide gas produced by Propionibacterium freudenreichii as it ferments lactate during ripening
Boiling the cheese curd
Penicillium mold growth
questions.correct_answer: Carbon dioxide gas produced by Propionibacterium freudenreichii as it ferments lactate during ripening
questions.explanation: Propionibacterium freudenreichii ferments lactate to propionic acid, acetic acid, and CO2 during the warm ripening stage of Swiss-type cheese; the slowly accumulating CO2 forms the characteristic round eyes as it diffuses through the curd.

questions.question: Souring (spoilage) of raw milk left unrefrigerated is typically caused by:
options: Growth of naturally occurring lactic acid bacteria that ferment lactose to lactic acid, eventually curdling the milk
Chemical oxidation of milk fat only
Loss of water from the milk
Growth of algae in the milk
questions.correct_answer: Growth of naturally occurring lactic acid bacteria that ferment lactose to lactic acid, eventually curdling the milk
questions.explanation: Left at ambient temperature, indigenous or contaminating lactic acid bacteria in raw milk multiply and ferment lactose to lactic acid; as acidity rises, casein denatures and coagulates, producing the classic souring/curdling of unrefrigerated milk.

questions.question: The standard plate count (aerobic colony count) of raw milk is an important quality indicator mainly because a high count reflects:
options: Excellent hygienic milking practice
Poor udder health, unsanitary milking/handling conditions, or inadequate cooling, all of which raise the risk of spoilage and reduce shelf life
The presence of added preservatives
The fat content of the milk
questions.correct_answer: Poor udder health, unsanitary milking/handling conditions, or inadequate cooling, all of which raise the risk of spoilage and reduce shelf life
questions.explanation: Elevated total bacterial counts in raw milk usually signal contamination from unclean equipment, poor animal hygiene, mastitis, or insufficient cooling after milking, all of which compromise milk quality and shelf life.

questions.question: Bovine mastitis, an udder infection that can compromise milk quality and safety, is most commonly caused by bacteria such as:
options: Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus agalactiae
Saccharomyces cerevisiae
Penicillium roqueforti
Lactobacillus bulgaricus
questions.correct_answer: Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus agalactiae
questions.explanation: Mastitis, inflammation of the mammary gland in dairy cattle, is most often caused by bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus agalactiae, which can contaminate milk and, in the case of S. aureus, produce heat-stable enterotoxin.

questions.question: A food-borne intoxication differs from a food-borne infection in that intoxication results from:
options: Ingestion of live pathogenic organisms that then multiply within the host's gut
Ingestion of a pre-formed microbial toxin already present in the food, so illness can occur even if no living organisms are consumed
Allergic reaction to a food protein
Physical injury from sharp food particles
questions.correct_answer: Ingestion of a pre-formed microbial toxin already present in the food, so illness can occur even if no living organisms are consumed
questions.explanation: In food intoxication, the causative agent is a toxin already produced by microbial growth in the food before consumption (e.g. staphylococcal enterotoxin, botulinum toxin); in a food infection, live pathogens are ingested and cause illness by infecting the host, often after an incubation period.

questions.question: Staphylococcal food poisoning, typically producing rapid-onset (1-6 hour) vomiting and diarrhoea after eating improperly refrigerated cream-filled or protein-rich foods, is caused by:
options: A heat-stable enterotoxin produced by Staphylococcus aureus during growth in the food before consumption
Live Staphylococcus aureus cells invading the intestinal wall
A neurotoxin produced by Clostridium botulinum
Salmonella endotoxin
questions.correct_answer: A heat-stable enterotoxin produced by Staphylococcus aureus during growth in the food before consumption
questions.explanation: S. aureus growing in mishandled food secretes a heat-stable enterotoxin; because the toxin itself survives normal cooking/reheating and acts rapidly on the gut, symptoms of vomiting and diarrhoea typically appear within just a few hours of ingestion.

questions.question: Botulism, a rare but potentially fatal form of food poisoning associated with improperly processed home-canned low-acid foods, results from ingestion of a potent neurotoxin produced by:
options: Clostridium botulinum
Bacillus cereus
Escherichia coli O157:H7
Campylobacter jejuni
questions.correct_answer: Clostridium botulinum
questions.explanation: Clostridium botulinum, an anaerobic spore-forming bacterium, produces botulinum toxin, one of the most potent known neurotoxins, when its spores germinate and grow in anaerobic, low-acid conditions such as improperly processed canned foods, blocking acetylcholine release and causing flaccid paralysis.

questions.question: Bacillus cereus food poisoning is notable for causing two distinct clinical syndromes: an emetic (vomiting) form linked to reheated rice, and a diarrhoeal form. The emetic form is caused by:
options: A heat-stable toxin (cereulide) formed in the food before consumption
Live invasive organisms penetrating the intestinal mucosa
A virus contaminating the rice
Aflatoxin contamination
questions.correct_answer: A heat-stable toxin (cereulide) formed in the food before consumption
questions.explanation: The emetic syndrome of B. cereus food poisoning is caused by cereulide, a heat-stable, pre-formed toxin that survives reheating (classically associated with cooked rice left at room temperature and then reheated), distinguishing it from the heat-labile enterotoxins responsible for the diarrhoeal form.

questions.question: Listeria monocytogenes is of particular food safety concern in ready-to-eat and refrigerated foods (e.g. soft cheeses, deli meats) because it:
options: Cannot survive refrigeration temperatures
Is psychrotrophic (able to grow slowly even at refrigeration temperatures) and can cause severe illness, including in pregnant women, newborns, and immunocompromised individuals
Only causes mild, self-limiting illness in all populations
Is destroyed by normal refrigeration alone
questions.correct_answer: Is psychrotrophic (able to grow slowly even at refrigeration temperatures) and can cause severe illness, including in pregnant women, newborns, and immunocompromised individuals
questions.explanation: Listeria monocytogenes can multiply, albeit slowly, at typical refrigeration temperatures, allowing it to reach infectious doses in stored ready-to-eat foods; it is especially dangerous to pregnant women (risking miscarriage/stillbirth), neonates, the elderly, and immunocompromised persons.

questions.question: Non-typhoidal Salmonella food poisoning is most commonly associated with consumption of contaminated:
options: Distilled water
Poultry, eggs, and undercooked meat
Refined sugar
Cooking oil
questions.correct_answer: Poultry, eggs, and undercooked meat
questions.explanation: Non-typhoidal Salmonella serovars are frequently associated with poultry, eggs, and undercooked meat, causing a self-limiting gastroenteritis after a typical incubation period of 12-72 hours.

questions.question: Escherichia coli O157:H7, an important food-borne pathogen associated with undercooked ground beef and contaminated produce, is dangerous mainly because it produces:
options: A heat-labile enterotoxin identical to that of Vibrio cholerae
Shiga-like (verotoxin) toxins that can damage blood vessels and cause haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS), particularly in children
Aflatoxin
No toxin at all; illness is due to allergic reaction
questions.correct_answer: Shiga-like (verotoxin) toxins that can damage blood vessels and cause haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS), particularly in children
questions.explanation: Enterohaemorrhagic E. coli O157:H7 produces Shiga-like toxins (verotoxins) that damage vascular endothelium, and in severe cases (especially in young children) can precipitate haemolytic uraemic syndrome, a serious kidney complication.

questions.question: In HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point) systems, a Critical Control Point (CCP) is defined as:
options: Any random point in the production process
A step in food production at which control can be applied and is essential to prevent, eliminate, or reduce a significant food safety hazard to an acceptable level
The point where the final product is packaged
A location used only for storing raw materials
questions.correct_answer: A step in food production at which control can be applied and is essential to prevent, eliminate, or reduce a significant food safety hazard to an acceptable level
questions.explanation: HACCP identifies specific points in a food process (CCPs) where control measures (e.g. a cooking temperature, a metal detector) can be applied and monitored to prevent or reduce an identified hazard to a safe level, forming the core of the preventive food safety system.

questions.question: The HACCP approach to food safety is fundamentally different from traditional end-product testing in that HACCP:
options: Relies solely on testing the finished product for pathogens before release
Is a preventive, systematic approach that identifies and controls hazards at each stage of production, rather than relying only on testing the finished product
Eliminates the need for any hygiene practices
Applies only to canned foods
questions.correct_answer: Is a preventive, systematic approach that identifies and controls hazards at each stage of production, rather than relying only on testing the finished product
questions.explanation: HACCP shifts food safety assurance from reactive, after-the-fact end-product testing to a proactive system that analyses hazards and builds in controls at each critical step of the production process, reducing the risk that unsafe product reaches consumers.

questions.question: Coliform bacteria are used as indicator organisms in food and dairy microbiology mainly to signal:
options: The presence of desirable fermentation organisms
Possible faecal contamination or inadequate sanitation/processing, since coliforms are common in the gut and environment and relatively easy to detect
The nutritional value of the food
The exact identity of any pathogen present
questions.correct_answer: Possible faecal contamination or inadequate sanitation/processing, since coliforms are common in the gut and environment and relatively easy to detect
questions.explanation: Coliform counts are used as a practical, easily measured indicator of sanitary quality; their presence, especially at elevated levels, suggests possible faecal contamination or lapses in hygiene/processing, even though coliforms themselves are not always pathogenic.

questions.question: Probiotics, as used in fermented dairy products and supplements, are defined as:
options: Any bacteria present in a food, whether beneficial or harmful
Live microorganisms which, when administered in adequate amounts, confer a health benefit on the host, e.g. certain Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium strains
Chemical preservatives added to extend shelf life
Toxins produced by spoilage organisms
questions.correct_answer: Live microorganisms which, when administered in adequate amounts, confer a health benefit on the host, e.g. certain Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium strains
questions.explanation: Probiotics are specific live microbial strains (commonly Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium species) that, when consumed in sufficient numbers, are documented to provide a health benefit to the host, such as supporting gut microbiota balance.

questions.question: Prebiotics differ from probiotics in that prebiotics are:
options: Live beneficial microorganisms themselves
Non-digestible food ingredients (often fibres/oligosaccharides) that selectively stimulate the growth or activity of beneficial bacteria already present in the gut
Antibiotics used to treat food-borne infections
Preservatives that kill all gut bacteria
questions.correct_answer: Non-digestible food ingredients (often fibres/oligosaccharides) that selectively stimulate the growth or activity of beneficial bacteria already present in the gut
questions.explanation: Prebiotics are substrates (such as certain oligosaccharides and fibres) that are selectively used by beneficial host microorganisms, thereby promoting their growth, in contrast to probiotics, which are the live beneficial organisms themselves.

questions.question: Nigerian traditional fermented food 'ogi' (a fermented maize/sorghum/millet gruel commonly used as a weaning food) relies primarily on fermentation by:
options: A mixed natural microflora dominated by lactic acid bacteria (e.g. Lactobacillus species) along with yeasts, during steeping and souring of the cereal
Penicillium roqueforti only
Escherichia coli O157:H7
Vibrio cholerae
questions.correct_answer: A mixed natural microflora dominated by lactic acid bacteria (e.g. Lactobacillus species) along with yeasts, during steeping and souring of the cereal
questions.explanation: Ogi production involves steeping cereal grains in water, during which indigenous lactic acid bacteria and yeasts spontaneously ferment the starch and sugars, souring the mash and contributing to its characteristic flavour and improved digestibility/preservation.

questions.question: Nigerian 'garri' processing from cassava tubers involves a fermentation step that is important partly because it helps to:
options: Increase the cyanogenic glycoside (toxic cyanide-releasing compound) content of the cassava
Reduce the cyanogenic glycoside content of the cassava through microbial and enzymatic action, along with grating, pressing, and roasting, lowering the risk of cyanide toxicity
Convert the cassava starch entirely into protein
Sterilise the cassava permanently
questions.correct_answer: Reduce the cyanogenic glycoside content of the cassava through microbial and enzymatic action, along with grating, pressing, and roasting, lowering the risk of cyanide toxicity
questions.explanation: During garri fermentation, microbial and plant enzymatic activity, combined with grating, dewatering under pressure, and subsequent roasting, break down and help remove cyanogenic glycosides naturally present in cassava, an important food safety step in cassava processing.

questions.question: Nigerian 'nono' (traditional fermented milk) is produced through spontaneous fermentation of fresh milk mainly by:
options: Naturally occurring lactic acid bacteria, which acidify and thicken the milk, similar in principle to yoghurt fermentation
Aspergillus flavus
Clostridium botulinum
Vibrio parahaemolyticus
questions.correct_answer: Naturally occurring lactic acid bacteria, which acidify and thicken the milk, similar in principle to yoghurt fermentation
questions.explanation: Nono is traditionally made by allowing fresh cow's milk to ferment spontaneously (sometimes back-slopped with a portion of a previous batch), with indigenous lactic acid bacteria souring and thickening the milk much as in other lactic-fermented dairy products.
